import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.12

by R. I. Grigorchuk

Does there exist a finitely generated semigroup $S$ with cancellation having
non-exponential growth and such that its group of left quotients $G = S^{-1}S$
(which exists) is a group of exponential growth?

An affirmative answer would give a positive solution to Problem 12 in
S. Wagon, *The Banach–Tarski Paradox*, Cambridge Univ. Press, 1985.

The growth function of a semigroup $S$ with respect to a finite generating set
$A$ counts the elements of $S$ that are products of at least one and at most $n$ elements of $A$.
Its exponential growth rate $\lim_{n \to \infty} \gamma(n)^{1/n}$ exists, and
whether it equals $1$ (non-exponential growth) or exceeds $1$ (exponential
growth) does not depend on the finite generating set. The same holds for the
growth function of a finitely generated group (`GromovPolynomialGrowth.GrowthFunction`).

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
- S. Wagon, *The Banach–Tarski Paradox*, Cambridge Univ. Press, 1985.
-/
namespace Kourovka.«10.12»
open Filter GromovPolynomialGrowth
open scoped Pointwise
section Semigroup
variable {S : Type*} [Semigroup S]

  | 0 => ∅
  | n + 1 => A ∪ A * semigroupBall A n
blocks.docstring:
The ball of radius `n` in a semigroup `S` with respect to a set `A ⊆ S`: the set of all
products of at least one and at most `n` elements of `A`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: GromovPolynomialGrowth.CayleyBall (groups only, uses inverses); Set pointwise pow (requires Monoid); Subsemigroup.closure (no length grading).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.12».semigroupBall
justification.why_needed: The ball of radius n in a semigroup w.r.t. a set A (products of 1..n elements of A). Semigroups have no identity, so List.prod, Set.pow (which need Monoid) and the repo's CayleyBall (which needs Group) are unavailable; defined recursively via pointwise Set multiplication.

def HasExponentialGrowth (f : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, c ^ n ≤ (f n : ℝ)
blocks.docstring:
A growth function `f : ℕ → ℕ` has exponential growth if it eventually dominates $c^n$ for
some $c > 1$, i.e. its exponential growth rate $\liminf_{n \to \infty} f(n)^{1/n}$ exceeds $1$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: GromovPolynomialGrowth.HasSuperPolynomialGrowth / HasPolynomialGrowth (polynomial, not exponential, and group-specific); Asymptotics.IsBigO (would need an extra constant and does not express a rate condition directly).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.12».HasExponentialGrowth
justification.why_needed: Exponential growth of a function ℕ → ℕ: ∃ c > 1 with c^n ≤ f n eventually (growth rate > 1). Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib defines exponential growth of a growth function.

blocks.name: HasExponentialGrowth
blocks.text:
/-- A growth function `f : ℕ → ℕ` has exponential growth if it eventually dominates $c^n$ for
some $c > 1$, i.e. its exponential growth rate $\liminf_{n \to \infty} f(n)^{1/n}$ exceeds $1$. -/

blocks.code:
def HasSubexponentialGrowth (f : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ c : ℝ, 1 < c → ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (f n : ℝ) ≤ c ^ n
blocks.docstring:
A growth function `f : ℕ → ℕ` has non-exponential (subexponential) growth if it is
eventually bounded by $c^n$ for every $c > 1$, i.e. $\limsup_{n \to \infty} f(n)^{1/n} \le 1$.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Asymptotics.IsLittleO of log f vs n (used ad hoc in ErdosProblems/1101 but not as a definition); Asymptotics.SuperpolynomialDecay (wrong notion).
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.12».HasSubexponentialGrowth
justification.why_needed: Non-exponential (subexponential) growth of a function ℕ → ℕ: for every c > 1, f n ≤ c^n eventually (growth rate 1). No existing definition in Mathlib or the repo; a test lemma proves it excludes HasExponentialGrowth.

blocks.name: HasSubexponentialGrowth
blocks.text:
/-- A growth function `f : ℕ → ℕ` has non-exponential (subexponential) growth if it is
eventually bounded by $c^n$ for every $c > 1$, i.e. $\limsup_{n \to \infty} f(n)^{1/n} \le 1$. -/
def HasSubexponentialGrowth (f : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ c : ℝ, 1 < c → ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (f n : ℝ) ≤ c ^ n

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_hasExponentialGrowth_of_hasSubexponentialGrowth {f : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hf : HasSubexponentialGrowth f) : ¬ HasExponentialGrowth f := by
  rintro ⟨c, hc, hcf⟩
  set d := (1 + c) / 2 with hd
  have hd1 : 1 < d := by rw [hd]; linarith
  have hdc : d < c := by rw [hd]; linarith
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := eventually_atTop.1 ((hf d hd1).and hcf)
  obtain ⟨hn, hn'⟩ := hN (N + 1) (Nat.le_succ N)
  have : c ^ (N + 1) ≤ d ^ (N + 1) := hn'.trans hn
  exact absurd this (not_le.2 (pow_lt_pow_left₀ hdc (by linarith) (Nat.succ_ne_zero N)))

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.12» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (S : Type) (_ : Semigroup S) (_ : IsCancelMul S) (A : Finset S),
      Subsemigroup.closure (A : Set S) = ⊤ ∧
      HasSubexponentialGrowth (semigroupGrowth (A : Set S)) ∧
      ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (ι : S →ₙ* G),
        Function.Injective ι ∧
        (∀ g : G, ∃ s t : S, g = (ι s)⁻¹ * ι t) ∧
        HasExponentialGrowth (GrowthFunction (ι '' A)) := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Does there exist a finitely generated semigroup $S$ with cancellation having non-exponential
growth and such that its group of left quotients $G = S^{-1}S$ (which exists) is a group of
exponential growth?

Here $S$ is a two-sided cancellative semigroup generated by a finite set $A$, and its growth
function with respect to $A$ has exponential growth rate $1$. The group of left quotients
$G = S^{-1}S$ is a group $G$ together with an injective homomorphism $\iota \colon S \to G$
such that every element of $G$ has the form $\iota(s)^{-1}\iota(t)$ with $s, t \in S$; its
existence is part of the hypothesis (it exists exactly when $S$ satisfies the left Ore
condition, and it is then unique up to isomorphism). Such a $G$ is generated as a group by
$\iota(A)$, and the question asks that its growth function with respect to $\iota(A)$ have
exponential growth rate $> 1$.

claims.decomposer_note: Single existence yes/no question: S is a finitely generated (two-sided) cancellative semigroup satisfying the left Ore condition so that the group of left quotients G = S^{-1}S exists (existence is a hypothesis, i.e. S embeds in a group G with every element of the form s^{-1}t); 'non-exponential growth' means the growth function of S w.r.t. a finite generating set has exponential growth rate 1 (subexponential, independent of the generating set), while G (automatically finitely generated by the generators of S and their inverses) must have exponential growth (rate > 1); the closing sentence about Wagon's Problem 12 is a remark on a consequence, not a further question.
claims.reviewer_why: c06 states the question faithfully and most cleanly: answer(sorry) ↔ ∃ semigroup S with two-sided cancellation (IsCancelMul on the same Mul), a finite semigroup generating set A (Subsemigroup.closure A = ⊤), non-exponential growth of S w.r.t. A (∀ c > 1, eventually γ_A(n) ≤ c^n, i.e. limsup γ^{1/n} ≤ 1, which is exactly growth rate 1 since γ ≥ 1), and a group G with an injective MulHom ι : S → G such that every g = (ι s)⁻¹ * ι t (literally G = S⁻¹S, existence as hypothesis; such G is unique up to iso so ∃ over G is harmless), with G of exponential growth w.r.t. ι(A) (∃ c > 1, eventually c^n ≤ Γ(n); ι(A) generates G, and the limit of Γ^{1/n} exists for groups so this is rate > 1). Semigroup ball = products of 1..n generators, proven finite; predicates on ℕ → ℕ with a proven mutual-exclusivity test lemma; reuses the repo's GromovPolynomialGrowth.GrowthFunction. Degenerate cases (empty S, finite S) yield no spurious witness. All candidates c01–c06, c08 are mathematically faithful and equivalent; c06 was preferred for readability, API lemmas, and style (no lines > 100 chars unlike c03/c08; no redundant instance diamond unlike c07 which quantifies separate Semigroup/LeftCancelSemigroup/RightCancelSemigroup structures on S). Only edit: one docstring wording fix ('at least one and at most n').

namespace Kourovka.«10.12»

open Filter GromovPolynomialGrowth
open scoped Pointwise

section Semigroup

variable {S : Type*} [Semigroup S]

/-- The ball of radius `n` in a semigroup `S` with respect to a set `A ⊆ S`: the set of all
products of at least one and at most `n` elements of `A`. -/
def semigroupBall (A : Set S) : ℕ → Set S
  | 0 => ∅
  | n + 1 => A ∪ A * semigroupBall A n

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem semigroupBall_zero (A : Set S) : semigroupBall A 0 = ∅ := rfl

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem semigroupBall_one (A : Set S) : semigroupBall A 1 = A := by
  simp [semigroupBall]

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem semigroupBall_two (A : Set S) : semigroupBall A 2 = A ∪ A * A := by
  simp [semigroupBall]

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem semigroupBall_finite {A : Set S} (hA : A.Finite) (n : ℕ) :
    (semigroupBall A n).Finite := by
  induction n with
  | zero => simp [semigroupBall]
  | succ n ih => exact hA.union (hA.mul ih)

/-- The growth function of a semigroup `S` with respect to a set `A ⊆ S`: `semigroupGrowth A n`
is the number of elements of `S` that are products of at most `n` elements of `A`. -/
noncomputable def semigroupGrowth (A : Set S) (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (semigroupBall A n).ncard

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem semigroupGrowth_zero (A : Set S) : semigroupGrowth A 0 = 0 := by
  simp [semigroupGrowth, semigroupBall]

@[category API, AMS 20]
theorem semigroupGrowth_one (A : Set S) : semigroupGrowth A 1 = A.ncard := by
  simp [semigroupGrowth, semigroupBall]

end Semigroup

/-- A growth function `f : ℕ → ℕ` has exponential growth if it eventually dominates $c^n$ for
some $c > 1$, i.e. its exponential growth rate $\liminf_{n \to \infty} f(n)^{1/n}$ exceeds $1$. -/
def HasExponentialGrowth (f : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ c : ℝ, 1 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, c ^ n ≤ (f n : ℝ)

/-- A growth function `f : ℕ → ℕ` has non-exponential (subexponential) growth if it is
eventually bounded by $c^n$ for every $c > 1$, i.e. $\limsup_{n \to \infty} f(n)^{1/n} \le 1$. -/
def HasSubexponentialGrowth (f : ℕ → ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ c : ℝ, 1 < c → ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (f n : ℝ) ≤ c ^ n

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem not_hasExponentialGrowth_of_hasSubexponentialGrowth {f : ℕ → ℕ}
    (hf : HasSubexponentialGrowth f) : ¬ HasExponentialGrowth f := by
  rintro ⟨c, hc, hcf⟩
  set d := (1 + c) / 2 with hd
  have hd1 : 1 < d := by rw [hd]; linarith
  have hdc : d < c := by rw [hd]; linarith
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := eventually_atTop.1 ((hf d hd1).and hcf)
  obtain ⟨hn, hn'⟩ := hN (N + 1) (Nat.le_succ N)
  have : c ^ (N + 1) ≤ d ^ (N + 1) := hn'.trans hn
  exact absurd this (not_le.2 (pow_lt_pow_left₀ hdc (by linarith) (Nat.succ_ne_zero N)))

/--
Does there exist a finitely generated semigroup $S$ with cancellation having non-exponential
growth and such that its group of left quotients $G = S^{-1}S$ (which exists) is a group of
exponential growth?

Here $S$ is a two-sided cancellative semigroup generated by a finite set $A$, and its growth
function with respect to $A$ has exponential growth rate $1$. The group of left quotients
$G = S^{-1}S$ is a group $G$ together with an injective homomorphism $\iota \colon S \to G$
such that every element of $G$ has the form $\iota(s)^{-1}\iota(t)$ with $s, t \in S$; its
existence is part of the hypothesis (it exists exactly when $S$ satisfies the left Ore
condition, and it is then unique up to isomorphism). Such a $G$ is generated as a group by
$\iota(A)$, and the question asks that its growth function with respect to $\iota(A)$ have
exponential growth rate $> 1$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.12» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ (S : Type) (_ : Semigroup S) (_ : IsCancelMul S) (A : Finset S),
      Subsemigroup.closure (A : Set S) = ⊤ ∧
      HasSubexponentialGrowth (semigroupGrowth (A : Set S)) ∧
      ∃ (G : Type) (_ : Group G) (ι : S →ₙ* G),
        Function.Injective ι ∧
        (∀ g : G, ∃ s t : S, g = (ι s)⁻¹ * ι t) ∧
        HasExponentialGrowth (GrowthFunction (ι '' A)) := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«10.12»

items: The group of left quotients G = S⁻¹S is modelled as an abstract group G together with an injective MulHom ι : S →ₙ* G such that every g ∈ G equals (ι s)⁻¹ * ι t, rather than via Mathlib's OreLocalization (which is a right-fraction construction for monoids, not semigroups). Such a G exists iff the cancellative semigroup S satisfies the left Ore condition and is unique up to isomorphism, so this is the standard meaning of '(which exists)'. The order (ι s)⁻¹ * ι t matches the notebook's S⁻¹S (left quotients).

Both growth conditions are stated with respect to a single existentially chosen finite generating set A of S (and its image ι '' A, which generates G as a group since every element of G is a left quotient of elements of S = ⟨A⟩). Growth type (exponential rate 1 vs > 1) is independent of the finite generating set, so ∃ A and ∀ A are equivalent; the repo's HasPolynomialGrowth uses the same ∃-style.

'Non-exponential growth' is formalised as HasSubexponentialGrowth: ∀ c > 1, eventually γ(n) ≤ c^n (i.e. limsup γ(n)^{1/n} ≤ 1, so the growth rate is 1). 'Exponential growth' of G is HasExponentialGrowth: ∃ c > 1, eventually c^n ≤ γ(n) (liminf γ(n)^{1/n} > 1). Since lim γ(n)^{1/n} exists for both semigroup and group growth functions (Fekete, via γ(m+n) ≤ γ(m)(1+γ(n)) for semigroups), these coincide with 'growth rate = 1' and 'growth rate > 1'. A test lemma shows the two predicates are mutually exclusive.

The semigroup growth function counts elements expressible as products of at least one and at most n generators (semigroupBall A 0 = ∅, semigroupBall A (n+1) = A ∪ A * semigroupBall A n); the ball is proven finite for finite A so Set.ncard is the genuine count. For G the repository's GromovPolynomialGrowth.GrowthFunction (symmetric Cayley ball of radius n) is reused.
IsCancelMul S (two-sided cancellation) is kept as an explicit hypothesis to match 'with cancellation', although it is implied by the embedding of S into the group G.

Both S and G live in universe Type, following the existing Kourovka files. The empty semigroup is excluded automatically (G contains 1 but there would be no s, t ∈ S), and a finite S yields a finite G without exponential growth, so no degenerate witness exists.

reviewer_notes: Single-slot problem; all eight candidates formalized it and compiled. Shared modelling (agreed with the decomposition notes): the group of left quotients is encoded by its defining property (S embeds in G via an injective semigroup hom, every element of G is s⁻¹t), existence being a hypothesis; growth is measured w.r.t. one existentially chosen finite generating set of S and its image in G, which is legitimate since exponential vs non-exponential growth is independent of the finite generating set (for semigroups too, via γ_B(n) ≤ γ_A(kn)). c01 (S as a Subsemigroup of G, limsup rates), c02/c07 (limsup rates in ℝ; bounded so no junk), c05 (Mathlib ExpGrowth.expGrowthSup = 0 / > 0) are also faithful but were not chosen: c07 introduces three unrelated algebraic structures on S (ugly, though harmless because cancellation follows from the embedding), c03/c08 have >100-char lines, c01/c02/c05/c07 lack API tests for bespoke definitions. The remark about Wagon's Problem 12 is a consequence, recorded only in the module docstring, not formalized. IsCancelMul is redundant given the embedding into G but kept to mirror 'with cancellation'.
statement: Does there exist a finitely generated semigroup $S$ with cancellation having non-exponential growth and such that its group of left quotients $G=S^{-1}S$ (which exists) is a group of exponential growth? An affirmative answer would give a positive solution to Problem 12 in (S. Wagon, The Banach–Tarski Paradox, Cambridge Univ. Press, 1985).
